thread:
maya: seeing steady queue depth growth for mosaic-8b in ap-southeast1 inlet over the last 10m, now hitting 1.2k per-shard. admission control started dropping lower-priority pslots. ops-bot fired a few alerts. anyone already looking?
ops-bot: ALERT ap-southeast1: model=mosaic-8b queue_depth > 1000 on shards [s-12,s-14,s-18]. admission_control=active. avg_wait_ms=620. link: https://grafana.redwood/ap-s/queue?m=mosaic-8b
sam: on it. quick sanity check: is this traffic spike from a single customer or broad?
maya: looks broad; traffic heatmap shows ~35% increase across routed keys, not a single tenant ramp.
li-chen: seeing corresponding GPU util bump and a handful of preemptions. tail latencies for small tokens up too. likely kv-cache miss storm after rolling restart?
rachel: did we recently roll a model variant or change cache TTLs? I remember a canary yesterday that touched prefix caching.
maya: not from model side; config change was a batcher tweak in apac autoscale policy around 03:10. that might reduce evictions but could increase inflight if not paired with admission throttle.
sam: grabbing `pslot` and `queue` metrics now. snippet: 
```
metric queue_depth_shard_s-12: 420 -> 1240 (10m)
metric avg_inflight_per_shard: 18 -> 67
metric pslot_wait_ms_p90: 80 -> 610
```

sam: hypothesis: ingress routing sent a concentrated set of short-seq requests causing KV cache churn and downstream backpressure; batcher enlarged window so more requests queued per GPU.
jorge: we should protect critical models first. propose three steps: 1) enable per-model rate-limiter to soft-cap mosaic-8b in ap-southeast1; 2) temporarily route excess to fallback region (ap-northeast1) for non-low-latency tiers; 3) revert the batcher window change if we confirm it's causal.
li-chen: +1 for routing fallback. I can toggle routing policy to drain ~40% of non-enterprise traffic to ap-northeast1 within 2m.
rachel: can we also increase ephemeral pslot allowance on dedicated pools? costy but buys time for hotshard. how many spare GPUs are free in apac spare pool?
sam: spare pool check: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="label=ephemeral-apac AND status=RUNNING"` shows 6 spare cards (enough for ~12 shards). scaling takes ~6-8m to warm. fallback routing is faster.
maya: do fallback + soft-rate-limit immediately. I'll hold on revert until we confirm metrics.
ops-bot: EXECUTE user=rachel action=toggle-routing target=ap-southeast1->ap-northeast1 percent=40 status=queued
rachel: started routing change now. ops-bot will confirm.
ops-bot: ACTION_COMPLETE user=rachel action=toggle-routing status=success details="40% diverted for non-sla-tier"
li-chen: p90 queue depth on s-12 down from 1240 -> 760 in ~120s. pslot wait p90 down to 320ms. good immediate improvement.
sam: still seeing one shard (s-18) with sticky backlog. running `kubectl describe pod p-batcher-s-18` — shows prolonged GC pauses on the batcher container and repeated KV cache reconnects. possible network flap to redis cluster?
jorge: check redis replicas in ap-southeast1. if cache connectivity is flaky that explains misses + backlog.
maya: redis-gw reports increased connection errors since 03:07. suspected network noisy neighbor on that AZ.
li-chen: I've opened a ticket with cloud-networking (SR #98124) and marked it P1. they confirmed packet loss ~0.8% on the AZ switch. asking for NIC rebind on affected hosts.
rachel: temporary mitigation: move KV cache endpoints for batchers from local redis to cross-region read-replica? riskier but can help while network is remediated. prefer we avoid config churn.
sam: short-term plan recap: 1) routing diversion 40% applied (done) 2) soft per-model rate-limit on mosaic-8b ap-southeast1 to 200 rps (sam to apply) 3) alert cloud-net and track SR (li-chen) 4) monitor shard s-18 health and consider live-evacuate pods off noisy hosts (maya/jorge)
maya: assigning: sam -> apply rate-limit and post exact curl command; li-chen -> follow up with networking and update SR; jorge -> prepare pod-drain playbook for noisy hosts; rachel -> confirm cost+scale runway if we decide to burn ephemeral GPUs. I'll keep channel updated.
sam: applying rate-limit now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/ratelimit -d '{"model":"mosaic-8b","region":"ap-southeast1","limit_rps":200}'` -> 202 accepted.
ops-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE user=sam action=ratelimit model=mosaic-8b region=ap-southeast1 limit=200 status=applied
li-chen: SR updated: cloud-networking investigating NIC rebind, ETA 22m. no immediate ETA for full fix.
jorge: starting live-evacuate for pods on host h-az3-007 that show redis packet drops. will use `drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` pattern. ETA ~6m to move 4 batcher pods.
maya: thanks. current queue depth across region down to ~540 avg. still higher than normal but stabilizing. keep an eye on p90 wait.
rachel: once this settles, we should add a playback test to catch KV cache miss storms during small config rolls. also add an automatic fallback rule to route 30% traffic off region if queue_depth>800 sustained for 3m.
sam: agree. I'll open a follow-up ticket for automation.
li-chen: noted. I'll post SR updates and escalate if network latency increases again.
maya: closing triage for now — will reopen if queue_depth climbs back above 900 on any shard. :thumbsup:
